name: Assembly (cc1)
comment: One grammar for all three of cc1's outputs. GAS and MASM disagree about almost everything - comment character, label form, directive spelling - so both sets are matched rather than guessing which file this is. The overlap is harmless: MASM has no .text, GAS has no PROC.

patterns.comment: GAS on x86 and arm64 uses # and //; MASM uses ;
patterns.name: comment.line.cc1asm

patterns.comment: GAS: a name at the start of a line followed by a colon. Local labels .L... included.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.label.cc1asm

patterns.comment: MASM: name PROC / name ENDP / name LABEL
MASM unwind directives carry the frame description ml64 turns into .pdata/.xdata
patterns.name: keyword.control.directive.unwind.cc1asm

patterns.comment: MASM's bare-word directives and data definitions
patterns.name: keyword.control.directive.cc1asm

patterns.comment: x86-64: the general registers in all four widths, plus the vector and segment sets
patterns.name: variable.language.register.x86.cc1asm

patterns.comment: arm64: x0-x30, w0-w30, the vector files, and the named ones
patterns.name: variable.language.register.arm64.cc1asm

patterns.comment: Anything left at the head of a statement is the mnemonic. Matching by position rather than by a list means an instruction this grammar has never heard of still colours correctly - which matters, because the backends are still growing.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.mnemonic.cc1asm
